summary: A 35-foot Aermotor tower on Lyon Mountain, built 1917; in use until 1988, officially closed 1989, still standing and reachable by a marked hiking trail.

staffing.status: sometimes staffed; the Town of Saranac and NYSDEC hire a summit steward each summer

access.note: The NHLR says the trail is well marked and signed; Wikipedia says hikers can reach the tower; the New York Almanack says it can be climbed. The tower stands in the Chazy Highlands Wild Forest, and the access road is seasonal.

visit.trail_note: A 6.8-mile round trip per the New York Almanack, starting at a parking area about one mile up a seasonal dirt road off Chazy Lake Road.

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Fire lookout station established without a tower, because the summit was bare
35-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower erected on the summit by the New York State Conservation Commission
Tower in use until the end of the 1988 fire season
Officially closed in early 1989; DEC judged that airplanes were more effective for spotting fires
Domtar, owner of the tower and surrounding land until January 2005, sold about 20,000 acres to The Nature Conservancy; the land later went to New York State
NYSDEC and the Student Conservation Corps replaced footings, landing boards, stairs, cab floor and safety netting; materials flown in by state police helicopter
NYS chapter of the Forest Fire Lookout Association agreed to maintain the trail and tower
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register January 23, 2017 as US 1174
Inside of the cab repainted to cover graffiti

evidence.quote: A fire lookout station was established in April 1910, without a fire tower, as the summit of Lyon Mountain was bare at that time.

evidence.supports: 1917 tower erected by the state conservation commission, 35 ft (11 m), Aermotor LS40 steel
evidence.quote: In 1917, the New York State Conservation Commission erected a 35-foot-tall (11 m) Aermotor LS40 steel fire lookout tower on the mountain.

evidence.supports: 1917 steel tower erected at the summit
evidence.quote: Lyon Mountain was designated a fire tower peak in 1917, when the 35-foot steel tower was erected at the summit.

evidence.supports: NHLR gives Aermotor LS-40 design and 1917 build year
evidence.quote: This 35' Aermotor LS-40 tower was built in 1917.

evidence.supports: in use until end of 1988, officially closed 1989
evidence.quote: The fire tower was in use until the end of 1988 and was officially closed in 1989.

evidence.supports: tower ceased operations at the end of the 1988 fire season
evidence.quote: The tower ceased fire lookout operations at the end of the 1988 fire season.

evidence.supports: closed early 1989 after DEC decided airplanes were more effective for spotting fires
evidence.quote: It was officially closed in early 1989, when the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation determined that airplanes were more effective for spotting fires than fire towers.

evidence.supports: Domtar owned the tower and surrounding land until January 2005
evidence.quote: The tower and surrounding land belonged to timber company Domtar until January 2005

evidence.supports: 2005 repairs by NYSDEC and Student Conservation Corps
evidence.quote: New footings, landing boards, stairs, cab floor and safety netting were put in place in 2005 through a joint effort of the NYSDEC and the Student Conservation Corp.

evidence.supports: materials flown in by police helicopter

evidence.supports: 2017 repainting of cab interior to cover graffiti
evidence.quote: In 2017 the inside of the fire tower cab was repainted to cover graffiti.

evidence.quote: A radio repeater is on the fire tower, with solar panels and antenna

evidence.quote: The Town of Saranac and the NYSDEC hire a summit steward each summer

evidence.quote: to greet visitors and inform them of fire tower history

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives the tower site as 3,813 ft (1,162 m); Wikipedia gives the summit as 3,820 ft (1,160 m); the Almanack says 3,830 feet. The record keeps the NHLR tower-site value, which matches the record.

sources.title: Recreation Highlight: Lyon Mountain Fire Tower

notes_for_editor: The build year (1917) and the 1988 end of service agree across the NHLR, Wikipedia and the Almanack; the 1910 station predates the tower and is noted. The record already has 1917 built and 2017 registration, both correct; no correction needed. Staffing and access come from an undated NHLR entry and a 2022 Almanack article, so a current check with NYSDEC or the Town of Saranac is advised before any visit. The NHLR says the 2005 repairs were by NYSDEC with the Student Conservation Corps. No new photos were added.
